name: QUERY
description: QUERY runs a Google Visualization API Query Language statement on a range of data. It's Google Sheets' most powerful data function — essentially SQL for your spreadsheet.
tldr: QUERY lets you run SQL-like commands on your spreadsheet data. Filter, sort, aggregate, pivot — all in one formula. It's the Swiss Army knife of Google Sheets data manipulation.

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The range of cells to query. Include header row if you want to reference columns by name.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: A query string using Google Visualization API Query Language (similar to SQL). E.g., 'SELECT A, B WHERE C > 100 ORDER BY B DESC'.

parameters.name: headers
parameters.description: Number of header rows at the top of data. -1 = auto-detect, 0 = no headers. Default is -1.

basicExample.description: Select all rows where the region is 'East' and sort by sales descending
basicExample.formula: =QUERY(A1:E50, "SELECT A, B, D WHERE C = 'East' ORDER BY D DESC", 1)
basicExample.explanation: SELECT A, B, D picks 3 columns. WHERE C='East' filters by region. ORDER BY D DESC sorts by sales. 1 header row.

advancedExamples.title: QUERY with aggregation (GROUP BY)
advancedExamples.description: Sum sales by region using GROUP BY
advancedExamples.formula: =QUERY(A1:E50, "SELECT C, SUM(D) GROUP BY C ORDER BY SUM(D) DESC", 1)
advancedExamples.explanation: GROUP BY C groups rows by region. SUM(D) totals sales per group. Results are sorted by total descending.

advancedExamples.title: QUERY with multiple conditions
advancedExamples.description: Filter for East region sales above $5000 in Q1
advancedExamples.formula: =QUERY(A1:F50, "SELECT A, B, D WHERE C='East' AND D>5000 AND F='Q1'", 1)
advancedExamples.explanation: Multiple WHERE conditions combined with AND. Each condition is evaluated independently before results are combined.

advancedExamples.title: QUERY with IMPORTRANGE for cross-sheet analysis
advancedExamples.description: Query data from another spreadsheet entirely
advancedExamples.explanation: IMPORTRANGE pulls data from another spreadsheet. QUERY then filters it. Use Col1, Col2 (not A, B) when querying IMPORTRANGE data.

howItWorks: QUERY treats your spreadsheet range like a database table. The query string uses a SQL-like language: SELECT chooses columns, WHERE filters rows, GROUP BY aggregates, ORDER BY sorts, LIMIT restricts row count. Column references use letters (A, B, C) when querying a direct range, or Col1, Col2, Col3 when querying computed arrays like IMPORTRANGE results. The function evaluates the query and returns a dynamic result set that spills into adjacent cells.

howToSteps.name: Set up your data range
howToSteps.text: Select the full range including headers (e.g., A1:E50). Headers allow column name references.

howToSteps.name: Write your query string
howToSteps.text: Use SQL-like syntax: SELECT columns, WHERE conditions, ORDER BY, GROUP BY. Enclose in quotes.

howToSteps.name: Specify header rows
howToSteps.text: Set headers parameter: 1 if one header row, -1 for auto-detect.

howToSteps.name: Enter the formula
howToSteps.text: Type =QUERY(range, "SELECT A WHERE B > 100", 1) in a cell with space for spilled results.

limitations: QUERY is exclusive to Google Sheets — there is no equivalent in Excel.
QUERY cannot reference columns by letter (A, B) when the data comes from IMPORTRANGE — use Col1, Col2 instead.
QUERY has limited date handling — dates must be formatted carefully in the query string.
Complex queries may be slow on very large datasets (10K+ rows).
QUERY doesn't support JOIN operations between different ranges.

commonErrors.cause: Referencing column by letter (A, B) when data comes from IMPORTRANGE or computed arrays
commonErrors.fix: Use Col1, Col2, Col3 notation for computed array sources. Letters only work with direct range references.

commonErrors.cause: WHERE condition doesn't match any rows, or date format is wrong
commonErrors.fix: Check that your conditions actually match data. For dates, use date 'YYYY-MM-DD' format in the query.

commonErrors.cause: Syntax error in the query string
commonErrors.fix: Verify SQL syntax: quotes around text values, proper SELECT/WHERE/ORDER BY structure, no typos.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: QUERY is a Google Sheets exclusive function — there is no direct Excel equivalent.
googleSheetsEquivalent.formula: =QUERY(A1:E50, "SELECT A, B WHERE C = 'East' ORDER BY B DESC", 1)
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: In Excel, use FILTER + SORT for similar functionality, or Power Query for advanced data manipulation.

faq.question: What's the Excel equivalent of QUERY?
faq.answer: There's no direct equivalent. FILTER + SORT can handle basic filtering and sorting. For aggregation (GROUP BY), use PivotTables or Power Query. For complex analysis, Power Query is the closest match.

faq.question: Can QUERY reference another sheet?
faq.answer: Yes. Use the sheet name in the range: =QUERY(Sheet2!A1:E50, ...) or use IMPORTRANGE for cross-spreadsheet data.

faq.question: How do I handle dates in QUERY?
faq.answer: Use the date keyword: WHERE A > date '2024-01-01'. The date must be in YYYY-MM-DD format regardless of your spreadsheet date formatting.

faq.question: Can QUERY do pivot tables?
faq.answer: Yes! Use PIVOT in the query: =QUERY(A1:E50, "SELECT C, SUM(D) GROUP BY C PIVOT B", 1) creates a pivot-like summary.

faq.question: Why does QUERY return Col1 instead of A?
faq.answer: When QUERY operates on computed arrays (IMPORTRANGE results, {array} literals), columns are referenced as Col1, Col2, etc. Letter references (A, B) only work with direct spreadsheet ranges.
